content_html:
Shopify vs WooCommerce: Which Is Better for Your Business?

Shopify vs WooCommerce is the most common platform choice for a new online store. Shopify is a hosted, all-in-one platform: you pay a monthly fee and get hosting, security and checkout built in. WooCommerce is a free plugin for WordPress: you own and run the whole store, so you get more control but also more responsibility. In short, choose Shopify for speed and simplicity, and WooCommerce for flexibility and content-led selling.

Shopify vs WooCommerce at a glance

ShopifyWooCommerce
SetupSign up and launch quicklyNeeds hosting, WordPress and setup
Monthly costPlan fee plus paid appsHosting, plugins and maintenance
ControlLimited to what Shopify allowsFull access to code and data
MaintenanceHandled by ShopifyYour team or agency
Content and bloggingBasicExcellent, through WordPress
Best forFast launches, small teamsCustom stores, content-heavy brands

Cost: launch vs long term

Shopify is usually cheaper to launch, because you skip hosting and server setup. However, its costs add up over time: the monthly plan, paid apps and, unless you use Shopify Payments where available, transaction fees. WooCommerce has no platform fee. Instead, you pay for hosting, premium plugins and someone to keep it updated. For a store with steady sales and many features, WooCommerce often costs less over three years. Our guide to ecommerce website development cost breaks down typical budgets in India.

Features and flexibility

Both platforms cover the basics well: product pages, variants, inventory, coupons, shipping rules and order management. The difference is in how far you can go. With Shopify, unusual features come from apps, and some things simply cannot be changed. With WooCommerce, a developer can build almost anything, such as custom pricing rules, B2B ordering or complex product options. On the other hand, more freedom means more ways to slow the site down if plugins are chosen badly.

SEO and content

Both can rank well on Google. Shopify handles technical basics automatically but fixes some URL patterns, such as /products/ and /collections/. WooCommerce gives full control over URLs, schema and content, and it sits on WordPress, which is still the strongest blogging tool. So if content marketing is central to your plan, WooCommerce has the edge. Our website SEO and performance page explains what matters most.

Payments in India

Indian shoppers expect UPI, cards, net banking, wallets and often cash on delivery. Both platforms support Indian gateways such as Razorpay, PayU and Cashfree through apps or plugins. Check the gateway's fees and settlement times, because they affect cash flow more than the platform does.

Maintenance and security

Shopify looks after hosting, updates and security for you. That is a big advantage for small teams. With WooCommerce, you must update WordPress, the theme and plugins, keep backups and watch security. Many stores solve this with a monthly maintenance plan. Learn more in our guide to website maintenance cost.

Scaling a growing store

Shopify scales smoothly for traffic, because Shopify runs the servers. WooCommerce scales well too, but it needs good hosting, caching and a clean setup. For very large or complex catalogs, both can be extended, and some brands move to headless commerce later.

Common migration mistakes

  • Changing product URLs without 301 redirects, which loses rankings.
  • Forgetting customer accounts and order history.
  • Not testing payment and shipping rules before launch.
  • Dropping product reviews and structured data.

Which should you choose?

Pick Shopify if you want to launch quickly, have a small team and value low maintenance. Pick WooCommerce if you want full control, already use WordPress or plan to grow through content. Still unsure? Our ecommerce development team can review your products and plans and recommend the right platform. You can also compare more options in our guide to the best ecommerce platform for new stores, or read Shopify's own pricing page for current plans.

Frequently asked questions

Shopify vs WooCommerce: which is better?

Shopify is better if you want a fast launch and little maintenance. WooCommerce is better if you want full control, a lower long-term cost and deep WordPress content.

Which is cheaper to run?

WooCommerce is usually cheaper over time because there is no platform fee, but you pay for hosting, plugins and upkeep. Shopify has a monthly plan plus app fees.

Which is better for SEO?

Both can rank well. WooCommerce gives more control over URLs and content, while Shopify is simpler but has a fixed URL structure.

Can I move from Shopify to WooCommerce later?

Yes. Products, customers and orders can be migrated, but set up 301 redirects for every old URL to keep your rankings.
